#Text=Tesee.
#Text=The old man viewed his visitor with great earnestness, having
#Text= never beheld but one white man before, whom Mr.
#Text=Park discovered to be
#Text= Major Houghton.
#Text=He appeared to disbelieve what Mr.
#Text=Park asserted, in
#Text= answer to his inquiries concerning the motives that induced him to
#Text= explore the country, and told him that he must go to Kooniakary to
#Text= pay his respects to the king, but desired to see him again before he
#Text= left Tesee.
#Text=Tesee is a large unwalled town, fortified only by a sort of citadel,
#Text= in which Tiggity Sego and his family reside.
#Text=The present inhabitants,
#Text= though possessing abundance of cattle and corn, eat without scruple
#Text= rats, moles, squirrels, snakes, locusts, &c.
#Text=The attendants of Mr.
#Text=Park were one evening invited to a feast, where making a hearty meal
#Text= of what they thought to be fish and kouskous, one of them found a
#Text= piece of hard skin in the dish, which he brought away with him, to
#Text= show Mr.
#Text=Park what sort of fish they had been eating.
#Text=On examining
#Text= the skin, it was discovered they had been feasting on a large snake.
#Text=Another custom, which is rigidly adhered to, is, that no woman is
#Text= allowed to eat an egg, and nothing will more affront a woman of Tesee
#Text= than to offer her an egg.
#Text=The men, however, eat eggs without scruple.
#Text=interfered, and told them that he would not see the king  '  s stranger
#Text= ill treated while under his protection, but that in the morning he
#Text= should be sent about his business.
#Text=This somewhat appeased their
#Text= clamour, but they compelled Mr.
#Text=Park to ascend a high seat by the
#Text= door of the mosque, that every one might see him, where he remained
#Text= till sunset, when he was conducted to a neat little hut, with a small
#Text= court before it; but the Moors climbed in crowds over the mud walls,
#Text= to see the white man perform his evening devotions, and eat eggs.
#Text=The
#Text= first demand was positively declined, but he professed his utmost
#Text= readiness to comply with the second; the dooty immediately brought
#Text= seven hens  '   eggs, but was much surprised that Mr.
#Text=Park would not eat
#Text= them raw, as it is a prevalent opinion in the interior of Africa,
#Text= that Europeans subsist chiefly on this diet.
#Text=His reluctance to
#Text= partake of this fare exalted him in the eyes of his sage visitants;
#Text= his host accordingly killed a sheep, and gave him a plentiful supper.
#Text=Mr.
#Text=Park  '  s route now lay through woods, much infested with all kinds
#Text= of wild animals.
#Text=On one occasion, his guide suddenly wheeled his
#Text= horse round, calling out (_Warra billi billi_, a very largo lion.)
#Text=Mr.
#Text=Park  '  s steed was ill fitted to convey him from the scene of
#Text=similar to rice.
#Text=As the provisions of the coffle were not exhausted,
#Text= kouskous was dressed for supper, and several villagers were invited
#Text= to partake; meanwhile one of the schoolmaster  '  s boys, who had fallen
#Text= asleep under the bentang, was carried off during the night; but the
#Text= thief, finding that his master  '  s residence was only three days  '
#Text= journey distant, thinking he could not be retained with security,
#Text= after stripping him, suffered him to return.
#Text=They now crossed the Black River by a bridge of a curious
#Text= construction.
#Text=Several tall trees are fastened together by the tops,
#Text= which float on the water, while the roots rest on the rocks on each
#Text= side of the river; these are covered with dry bamboos, and the whole
#Text= forms a passage, sloping from each end towards the middle, so as to
#Text= resemble an inverted arch.
#Text=In the rainy season the bridge is carried
#Text= away, but the natives constantly rebuilt it, and on that account
#Text= exact a small tribute from every passenger.
#Text=Being informed that, two hundred Jalonkas had assembled to intercept
#Text= and plunder the coffle, they altered their course, and about midnight
#Text= arrived at a town called Koba.
#Text=They now discovered that a free man
#Text=by whom they were ransomed; and he understood from the Moors
#Text= themselves, that they were not allowed to go in large bodies to
#Text= Timbuctoo.
#Text=This statement bears on the face of it a certain degree of
#Text= improbability; but it loses that character when it is considered that
#Text= Timbuctoo, although it is become, in consequence of its frontier
#Text= situation, the port, as it were, of the caravans from the north,
#Text= which could not return across the desert the same season, if they
#Text= were to penetrate deeper into Soudan, is yet, with respect to the
#Text= trade itself, probably only the point whence it diverges to Houssa,
#Text= Tuarick, &c. on the east, and to Walet, Jinnie, and Sego, on the west
#Text= and south, and not the mart where the merchandise of the caravans is
#Text= sold in detail.
#Text=Such Moors, therefore, as did not return to Barbary
#Text= with the returning caravan, but remained in Soudan until the
#Text= following season, might be expected to follow their trade to the
#Text= larger marts of the interior, and to return to Timbuctoo only to meet
#Text= the next winter  '  s caravans.
#Text=Adams arriving at Timbuctoo in February,
#Text= and departing in June, might therefore miss both the caravans
#Text= themselves and the traders, who remained behind in Soudan; and, on
#Text= the same principle, Park might find Moors carrying on an active trade
#Text= in the summer at Sansanding, and yet there might not be one at
#Text=season could not be far distant, a period, in which travelling is
#Text= very difficult and trying to European constitutions.
#Text=It is clear,
#Text= therefore, that it would have been prudent to remain at Goree or
#Text= Pisania, till that season had passed; but in Mr.
#Text=Park  '  s enthusiastic
#Text= state of mind, it would have been extremely painful to linger so long
#Text= on the eve of his grand and favorite undertaking.
#Text=He hoped, and it
#Text= seemed possible, that before the middle of June, when the rains
#Text= usually began, he might reach the Niger, which could then be
#Text= navigated without any serious toil or exposure.
#Text=He departed,
#Text= therefore, with his little band from Pisania, on the 4th May, and
#Text= proceeded through Medina, along the banks of the Gambia.
#Text=With so
#Text= strong a party, he was no longer dependent on the protection of the
#Text= petty kings and mansas, but the Africans seeing him so well provided,
#Text= thought he had now no claim on their hospitality; on the contrary,
#Text= they seized every opportunity to obtain some of the valuable articles
#Text= which they saw in his possession.
#Text=Thefts were practised in the most
#Text= audacious manner; the kings drove a hard bargain for presents; at one
#Text= place, the women, with immense labour had emptied all the wells, that
#Text= they might derive an advantage from selling the water.

#Text= quietly to these little annoyances, Mr.

#Text=The first day of spring is at Sockna a day of general rejoicing.
#Text=It
#Text= is then the custom, to dress out little tents or bowers on the tops
#Text= of the houses, decorating them with carpets, _jereeds_, shawls, and
#Text= sashes.
#Text=A gaudy handkerchief on a pole, as a standard, completes the
#Text= work, which is loudly cheered by the little children, who eat, drink,
#Text= and play during the day in these covered places, welcoming the
#Text= spring by songs, and crying continually, "O welcome spring, with
#Text= pleasure bring us plenty."
#Text=The women give entertainment in their
#Text= houses, and the day is quite a holiday.
#Text=From the top of the houses in
#Text= which Captain Lyon lodged, these little bowers had a very pretty
#Text= effect, every roof in the town being ornamented with one.
#Text=Four ears
#Text= of corn were this day seen perfectly ripe, which was very early for
#Text= the season.
#Text=The gardens here are excellent, compared with the others
#Text= in Fezzan.
#Text=Ten miles east by south from Sockna is the town of Hoon.
#Text=It is
#Text= smaller than Sockna, but is built and walled in the same manner.
#Text=It
#Text= has three gates, three mosques, and a large building, which is
#Text= dignified with the name of a castle, but it does not appear to have
#Text= even a loop-hole for musketry.
#Text=The palm groves and gardens come up
#Text=a rough nest, in which she covers from fourteen to eighteen eggs, and
#Text= regularly sits on them, in the same manner as the common fowl does on
#Text= her chickens, the male occasionally relieving the female.
#Text=[Footnote]
#Text= It is during the breeding season that the greatest numbers are
#Text= procured, the Arabs shooting the old ones on their nests.
#Text=[Footnote: There is one peculiarity attending the ostrich, which is,
#Text= that although the female lays from about twenty-five to thirty eggs,
#Text= yet she only sits upon about fifteen, throwing the remainder outside
#Text= the nest, where they remain until the young ones are hatched, and
#Text= these eggs form the first food of the young birds.
#Text=--EDITOR.]
#Text=On the 22d April, Captain Lyon and his companions left Sockna, in
#Text= company with Sultan Mukni, for Mourzouk, which they entered upon the
#Text= 4th May.
#Text=The whole way is an almost uninterrupted succession of stony
#Text= plains and gloomy wadys, with no water but that of wells, generally
#Text= muddy, brackish, or bitter, and at fearful intervals.
#Text=On the first
#Text= evening, the place of encampment was a small plain, with no other
#Text= vegetation than a few prickly _talk_ bushes, encircled by high
#Text= mountains of basalt, which gave it the appearance of a volcanic
#Text=on the next morning, and leaving an Arab castle to the south-east,
#Text= and some table-top hills, they arrived at Kasrowa by three in the
#Text= afternoon.
#Text=On the 9th December, they were to arrive at Tegerhy.
#Text=The Arabs
#Text= commenced skirmishing as soon as they came within sight of it, and
#Text= kept it up in front of the town for half an hour after their arrival.
#Text=They were to halt here for a day or two, for the purpose of taking in
#Text= the remainder of their dates and provisions, and never was halt more
#Text= acceptable.
#Text=Almost the whole of the party were afflicted with
#Text= illness; the servants were all so ill, that one of the negro women
#Text= made them a mess of kouscasou, with some preserved fat, which had
#Text= been prepared in Mourzouk, it was a sorry meal, for the fat was
#Text= rancid, and although tired and not very strong, Major Denham could
#Text= not refuse an invitation about nine at night, after he had laid down
#Text= to sleep, to eat camels  '   heart with Boo Khaloom; it was woefully hard
#Text= and tough, and the major suffered the next morning from indulging too
#Text= much at the feast.
#Text=The Tibboos and Arabs kept them awake half the night with their
#Text=country, so soon as debility or sickness comes upon him.
#Text=Towards the evening, when the wind became hushed, and the sky
#Text= re-assumed its bright and truly celestial blue, the Tibboo sheik, and
#Text= about thirty of his people, male and female, returned; but their
#Text= supplies were very scanty for a kafila of nearly three hundred
#Text= persons.
#Text=The sweet milk turned out to be nothing but sour camel  '  s
#Text= milk, full of dirt and sand; and the fat was in small quantities, and
#Text= very rancid.
#Text=They, however, purchased a lean sheep for two dollars,
#Text= which was indeed a treat.
#Text=Some of the girls who brought the milk were really pretty, as
#Text= contrasted with the extreme ugliness of the men.
#Text=They were different
#Text= from those of Bilma, were more of a copper colour, with high
#Text= foreheads, and a sinking between the eyes.
#Text=They have fine teeth, and
#Text= are smaller and more delicately formed than the Tibboos who inhabit
#Text= the towns.
#Text=It is quite surprising with what terror these children of the desert
#Text= view the Arabs, and the idea they have of their invincibility, while
#Text=although only three in number, the natives flew in all directions.
#Text=On their approaching the town, they beckoned to them, and got off
#Text= their horses, for the purpose of giving them confidence, and sat down
#Text= under the shade of a large tamarind tree.
#Text=An old negro, who spoke a
#Text= little Arabic, was the first who ventured to approach; seeing that he
#Text= was not ill-treated, the others soon followed his example.
#Text=Major
#Text= Denham begged a little sour milk, a most refreshing beverage after a
#Text= hot ride, but none was to be found, until they were assured that it
#Text= should be paid for, and at the sight of the dollar they all jumped
#Text= and skipped like so many monkeys.
#Text=Major Denham now began to eat some
#Text= biscuit which he had in his saddle cloth, which created much
#Text= astonishment, and the first to whom he offered some, refused to eat
#Text= it.
#Text=One, rather bolder than the rest, put a small piece in his mouth,
#Text= and pronounced it good, with such extravagant gestures, that the
#Text= visitors all became clamorous.
#Text=The major refused for a long time the
#Text= man, who had been suspicious at first, to the great amusement of the
#Text= rest, who seemed to relish the joke amazingly.
#Text=The little nest of thatched huts in which they lived, was most
#Text= beautifully situated on a rising spot, in the midst of a rich and
#Text=and remounted, to receive the sheik  '  s orders, and they were not to
#Text= proceed beyond Woodie until his pleasure was known.
#Text=So jealous and
#Text= suspicious are these negro princes of the encroachments of the Arabs,
#Text= that divers were the speculations as to whether the sheik would or
#Text= would not allow the Arabs to proceed with the party nearer his
#Text= capital.
#Text=A weekly fsug, or market, was held about a mile from the town, and
#Text= the women, flocking from the neighbouring negro villages, mounted on
#Text= bullocks, who have a thong of hide passed through the cartilage of
#Text= the nose when young, and are managed with great ease, had a curious
#Text= appearance.
#Text=A skin is spread on the animal  '  s back, upon which, after
#Text= hanging the different articles they take for sale, they mount
#Text= themselves.
#Text=Milk, sour and sweet, a little honey, lowls, gussub, and
#Text= gafooly, are amongst their wares; fat and _meloheea_ (ochra), a green
#Text= herb, which, with the bazeen, all negroes eat voraciously, and indeed
#Text= Christians too, as was afterwards experienced.
#Text=The men brought oxen,
#Text= sheep, goats, and slaves; the latter were few in number, and in
#Text= miserable condition.
#Text=When quite fatigued, Major Denham determined on making for some huts,
#Text= and begged a little milk, sweet or sour.
#Text=No knowing landlady of a
#Text= country ever scanned the character of her customer more than did this
#Text= untaught, though cunning negro, who was found there.
#Text=He first denied
#Text= that he had any, notwithstanding the bowls were scarcely ten paces
#Text= behind him, and then asked, what they had got to pay for it?
#Text=Major
#Text= Denham had in reality nothing with him; and after offering his pocket
#Text= handkerchief, which was returned to him, as not worth any thing, he
#Text= was about to depart, though ten long miles from the tents, thirsty as
#Text= he was, when the Arab pointed to a needle, which was sticking in the
#Text= major  '  s jacket; for this and a white bead, which the Arab produced,
#Text= they had a bowl of fine milk and a basket of nuts, which refreshed
#Text= them much.
#Text=On their way to the tents, they saw a flock of at least
#Text= five hundred pelicans, but could not get near enough to fire at them.
#Text=On the 11th, two of the sheik  '  s officers arrived, with letters and a
#Text= present of goroo nuts of Soudan; they have a pleasant bitter taste,
#Text= and are much esteemed by all the Tripoli people.
#Text=These letters
#Text= pressed Boo Khaloom to continue his march towards Kouka, with all his
#Text= people, a very great proof of his confidence in the peaceable
#Text=moment, but the beast, after looking carelessly at him, brushed past
#Text= his legs, broke the ring, overturning several who stood before him,
#Text= and bounded off to another part, where there were fewer people.
#Text=It remained that Major Denham should be introduced to the sultan, in
#Text= his royal residence at Birnie, where all the real state and pomp of
#Text= the kingdom, with none of its real power were concentrated.
#Text=On the
#Text= 2nd March, the English accompanied Boo Khaloom to that city, and on
#Text= their arrival, the following day was fixed for the interview.
#Text=Fashion
#Text= even in the most refined European courts, does not always follow the
#Text= absolute guidance of taste or reason, and her magic power is often
#Text= displayed in converting deformities into beauties, but there is
#Text= certainly no court, of which the taste is so absurd, grotesque, and
#Text= monstrous, as that to which Major Denham was now introduced.
#Text=An
#Text= enormous protruding belly, and a huge misshapen head, are the two
#Text= features, without which it is vain to aspire to the rank of a
#Text= courtier, or fine gentleman.
#Text=The form, valued perhaps as the type of
#Text= abundance and luxury, is esteemed so essential, that where nature has
#Text= not bestowed, and the most excessive feeding and cramming cannot
#Text= supply it, wadding is employed, and a false belly produced, which in
#Text=on his first entry, and for a quarter of a mile scarcely appeared a
#Text= city at all.
#Text=Even in its more crowded quarters, the houses rose
#Text= generally in clusters, separated by stagnant pools.
#Text=The inhabited
#Text= part on the whole, did not comprise more than a fourth of the space
#Text= enclosed by the walls, the rest consisted of fields, gardens, and
#Text= swamps; however, as the whole circuit is fifteen miles, there is
#Text= space for a population moderately estimated, to be between thirty or
#Text= forty thousand.
#Text=The market is held on a neck of land, between two
#Text= swamps, by which, during the rains, it is entirely overflowed, but in
#Text= the dry season it is covered with sheds of bamboo, arranged into
#Text= regular streets.
#Text=Different quarters are allowed for the several kinds
#Text= of goods; some for cattle, others for vegetables, while fruits of
#Text= various descriptions, so much neglected in Bornou, are here displayed
#Text= in profusion.
#Text=The fine cotton fabrics of the country are sold either
#Text= in webs, or in what are called tobes and Turkadees, with rich silken
#Text= strips or borders ready to be added.
#Text=Amongst the favourite articles
#Text= are goora or kolla nuts, which are called African coffee, being
#Text= supposed to give a peculiar relish to the water drunk after them; and
#Text= crude antimony, with the black tint of which every eyebrow in Houssa
#Text= must be dyed.
#Text=The Arabs also dispose here of sundry commodities that
#Text=in the mouth so much of that impression, that a glass of vinegar
#Text= tastes like sweet wine, and the sourest lemon like a sweet orange;
#Text= sugar is quite an unnecessary article in tea or coffee; in fact, the
#Text= most nauseous drug seems sweet to whomever chews this fruit, and its
#Text= effect is not worn away until after several meals.
#Text=It is generally
#Text= called the miraculous berry, and whoever eats of it in the morning,
#Text= must be content at least for that day to forego the flavour of every
#Text= kind of food, whether animal or vegetable, for all will be alike
#Text= saccharine to the palate, and the most ridiculous effect is often
#Text= produced by playing tricks upon those, who are not aware of its
#Text= peculiar property.
#Text=Lander himself was one of the dupes, and he
#Text= relates, that the first time he partook of one of these berries, he
#Text= thought himself under the influence of witchcraft--the fowl of which
#Text= he partook at dinner seemed to him as if it had been soaked in a
#Text= solution of sugar--the lime juice appeared to him as if it were mixed
#Text= with some saccharine matter--his biscuit tasted like a bun--and
#Text= although he was convinced that he had not put any sugar into his
#Text= grog, it seemed to him as if it had been sweetened by the first maker
#Text= of punch in his native country.

#Text= other domestic slaves.
#Text=The food of the slave and the free is nearly
#Text= the same.
#Text=The greatest man or woman in the country is not ashamed, at
#Text= times, to let the slaves eat of the same dish; but a woman is never
#Text= allowed to eat with a man.
#Text=With a people, who have neither
#Text= established law nor government, it is surprising that they are so
#Text= good and moral as they are; it is true, they will cheat if they can,
#Text= but amongst the civilized nations, who have both laws and government,
#Text= cheating is by no means a rare occurrence, and by those too, who are
#Text= the loudest in the professions of their honesty and integrity.
#Text=The country round Koolfu is a level plain, well cultivated, and
#Text= studded with little walled towns and villages along the banks of the
#Text= May Yarrow, and of a little river running into it from the north.
#Text=Between the walled towns of Bullabulla and Rajadawa, the route passed
#Text= through plantations of grain, indigo, and cotton; the soil clay mixed
#Text= with sand, with here and there large blocks of sandstone, containing
#Text= nodules of iron and veins of iron-stone.
#Text=At five days from Koolfu, the route entered at the town of Wazo, or
#Text=the said precious head and legs, and to him they were finally
#Text= committed by the disappointed eunuch, who could hardly forbear
#Text= weeping on the occasion; these relics are considered extremely
#Text= valuable as a charm.
#Text=The chief sent them a goat, a quantity of bananas, a dish of pounded
#Text= or rather mashed yam with gravy, and a large basket of _caffas_.
#Text=These are a kind of pudding, made into little round balls from
#Text= bruised Indian corn, which is first boiled to the consistence of
#Text= thick paste.
#Text=From being made entirely of coarse flour and water, they
#Text= have an insipid taste when new, but when kept for a day or two, they
#Text= become sour, and in this state are eaten by the natives.
#Text=There are
#Text= several deep wells in the town, but most of them are dried up, so
#Text= that water is exceedingly scarce, and it is sold in the market-place
#Text= to the inhabitants.
#Text=They were daily accosted on the road with such
#Text= salutations as these, "I hope you go on well on the path," "success
#Text= to the king  '  s work," "God bless you white men," "a blessing on your
#Text= return, &c."
#Text=They remained the whole of the 28th at Chaadoo, in order to give the
#Text=dismounted, and after a laborious ascent, which occupied them three
#Text= quarters of an hour, at length reached the top.
#Text=Stones and blocks of
#Text= granite interrupted their path, so that it became a very difficult
#Text= matter to force the horses along before them; they fell repeatedly,
#Text= but without materially injuring themselves.
#Text=The name of the town was Chekki; their arrival was rather unexpected,
#Text= and therefore the governor was not prepared to receive them, and they
#Text= sat down under a tree, until they were tired of waiting.
#Text=At length, a
#Text= man came to conduct them to his residence, which was but a little way
#Text= from the tree, under which they were reposing, when a tumultuous rush
#Text= was made by the inhabitants to precede them into the yard, and
#Text= notwithstanding the presence of their chief, they so surrounded the
#Text= travelling party as to prevent a particle of fresh air from reaching
#Text= them.
#Text=The governor received them with bluntness, but not unkindly,
#Text= though without much demonstration of good-will.
#Text=While in his yard, he
#Text= regaled them with water, and afterwards sent them a large calabash of
#Text= _foorah_ sweetened with honey to their lodgings, which did not taste
#Text= unlike thick gruel or _burgoo_, as it is termed in Scotland.
#Text=It is
#Text= made of a corn called goorah, is very palatable, and is in general
#Text=intersects the latter city.
#Text=Bòhoo was formerly the metropolis of
#Text= Youriba, but about half a century ago, the reigning prince preferring
#Text= the plain at Katunga, the seat of government was transferred there,
#Text= since which Bòhoo has materially declined in wealth, population, and
#Text= consequence, although it is still considered a place of great
#Text= importance, and the second town in the kingdom.
#Text=It is bounded on all
#Text= sides by hills of gradual ascent, which are prettily wooded, and
#Text= commands an extensive horizon.
#Text=The land in the vicinity of the town
#Text= presents a most inviting appearance, by no means inferior to any part
#Text= of England in the most favourable season of the year.
#Text=It appears to
#Text= be duly appreciated by the Fellatas, so great a number of whom reside
#Text= with their flocks in different parts, that the minister candidly
#Text= declared he could not give any information of their amount.
#Text=These
#Text= foreigners sell their milk, butter, and cheese in the market at a
#Text= reasonable rate.
#Text=The latter is made into little cakes about an inch
#Text= square, and when fried in butter is very palatable.
#Text=It is of the
#Text= consistence and appearance of the white of an egg, boiled hard.
#Text=Agreeably to the promise which Richard Lander made to the chief, he
#Text= left his brother to the care of old Pascoe and his wife, and hastened
#Text=Wowow.
#Text=Unwilling as the Landers always were to infringe upon the observance
#Text= of the Sabbath, they were nevertheless compelled on Sunday, May 30th,
#Text= to submit to the mortification of cleaning and polishing a sword and
#Text= pistol, which were sent them for that purpose by the king, against
#Text= the approaching mahommedan festival.
#Text=Yarro shortly afterwards sent
#Text= them a turkey, and one of his women presented them with a roasted
#Text= badger, a quantity of yams, &c. for the use of one of their people.
#Text=On this evening, the wives of the king unanimously bestowed a severe
#Text= reprimand on their royal husband for neglecting to offer them a
#Text= portion of a bottle of rum, which was given to him on the preceding
#Text= day.
#Text=The ladies scolded so lustily, that the noise was heard outside
#Text= the wall surrounding their huts, which led them to make the
#Text= discovery.
#Text=To appease the indignation of the irascible ladies, and to
#Text= reconcile them to the loss of so great a dainty as a glass of rum,
#Text= they were presented with a few beads, and some other trifles, but
#Text= still it was evident that these fancy articles bore no comparison in
#Text= the eyes of the ladies with the exquisite relish of the spirituous
#Text= liquid.
#Text=ignorance of the poor creatures, but such is their firm belief.
#Text=They had pursued their course in this manner, which had been
#Text= principally to the west, till about three in the afternoon, when they
#Text= came to a branch of the river about two hundred yards wide, and
#Text= seeing a small village at a short distance before them, they stopped
#Text= there for the purpose of obtaining some dried fish.
#Text=Having supplied
#Text= their wants and proceeded on, about an hour afterwards they again
#Text= stopped, that their people might take some refreshment.
#Text=Boy very
#Text= kindly presented Lander with a large piece of yam, reserving to
